Match: match_0066
Innings: 1
Fields:
- inn1.total_runs

Commentary:
Good morning from Brookfield Academy Ground at Riverside, where Northmere won the toss, chose to field, and then controlled almost every meaningful piece of the cricket that was actually completed before the match was abandoned, even though the scorecard also shows enough extras to remind you that this was not a perfectly clean bowling session. Southwell reached 64 for 5 in 19.2 overs, and because no chase ever happened, the only responsible way to read the match is through that interrupted first innings: Northmere had the better of the morning, Southwell were still technically alive with Jasper Cole unbeaten, but the batting side had not yet found a stand strong enough to change the direction of the game. The opening overs gave Northmere exactly the kind of grip a fielding side wants after choosing to bowl first.

Match: match_0085
Innings: 1
Fields:
- inn1.total_runs

Commentary:
At Central Academy Ground in Eastport, Metrovale won the toss, chose to field, and then spent most of Bayport ’s innings keeping the game in that awkward middle zone where the batting side never quite collapses and never quite breaks free either, which is why Bayport’s 226 for 9 from the full fifty overs felt competitive but not fully secure, a total made through repair after repair rather than one clean act of dominance. The start was immediately uncomfortable for Bayport, Nolan Hays never settling before Liam Carter bowled him, and Elias Carter left trying to turn a broken opening into something usable with Luca Rhodes coming in earlier than planned.
